extraction.name: Video-As-Prompt (VAP)
extraction.description: A unified semantic-controlled video generation framework that treats reference videos as prompts and enables plug-and-play in-context control via a mixture-of-transformers expert. VAP overcomes limits of structure-controlled methods (e.g., inappropriate pixel-wise priors) and task/condition-specific designs (e.g., non-generalizable models), providing scalable semantic control and zero-shot generalizability. The framework leverages a reference video as a direct semantic prompt, guiding a frozen Video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) via a plug-and-play Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) expert. This architecture prevents catastrophic forgetting and is guided by a temporally biased position embedding that eliminates spurious mapping priors for robust context retrieval.
extraction.creator: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, Qiang Xu
extraction.publisher: ByteDance, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
extraction.citeAs: Video-As-Prompt: Unified Semantic Control for Video Generation
extraction.rai:dataCollection: VAP-Data was constructed by curating 2K high-quality reference images from the internet spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases. These images were then used with Image-to-Video visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU and Kling) and community LoRAs to create paired videos by matching each image to all compatible templates. The dataset includes over 100K curated samples across 100 semantic conditions, covering four primary categories: concept (entity transformation and interaction), style, motion (human and non-human), and camera movement.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reference images sourced from the internet, paired with videos generated using commercial models (VIDU, Kling) and community LoRAs as visual-effects templates.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were resized to 480x720 (832) and sampled at 49 frames at 16fps. The reference video, reference image, target video, and captions were encoded into latents by a VAE and text encoder. First frame tokens were concatenated with video tokens. A temporally biased Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) was applied to avoid spurious pixel-wise mapping priors, placing the reference before the target video along the temporal axis while keeping spatial indices unchanged.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were implicitly defined by the semantic conditions (e.g., concept, style, motion, camera) and the paired reference-target video structure. The dataset was designed to capture diverse semantic controls without explicit manual labeling, relying on the semantic alignment between reference and target videos.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The semantic alignment between reference and target videos was evaluated using a semantic-alignment score measured by Gemini-2.5-pro and GPT-5, ensuring consistency between the reference semantic condition and the generated video. Human preference rates were also collected to validate the alignment.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: VIDU, Kling, community LoRAs, and automated evaluation tools (Gemini-2.5-pro, GPT-5) for semantic alignment scoring.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released as part of the Video-As-Prompt framework. Versioning and maintenance details are not explicitly mentioned, but the framework is designed for scalability and zero-shot generalization, suggesting ongoing updates and potential expansion of semantic conditions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The framework targets semantic-controlled video generation for research, education, and creative prototyping, with explicit prohibitions against surveillance, impersonation, political persuasion, or other high-risk deployments. Misuse risks include identity impersonation, deepfake content, targeted harassment, deceptive political messaging, and generation of sexualized or violent media, which are mitigated by research-only release, default content filters, and acceptable-use policies.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset inherits biases from the commercial models (VIDU, Kling) and community LoRAs used for generation, which may include stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations (e.g., poor hand generation). The synthetic nature of the dataset may limit generalization to real-world scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include the synthetic and derived nature of the dataset, which may inherit biases and artifacts from source templates. The semantic conditions are relatively limited and synthetic, and the framework's performance depends on caption quality and structural similarity between reference and target subjects. Multi-reference prompting may lead to unwanted visual detail blending. The approach also introduces additional inference costs due to the added parameters in the Mixture-of-Transformers expert.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use cases include training, testing, and validation for semantic-controlled video generation tasks. The framework supports diverse downstream applications such as entity transformation, style transfer, motion imitation, camera control, and fine-grained attribute editing. Usage is restricted to research-only scenarios, with explicit prohibitions against abusive or unlawful applications.
